activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Asymptotes of a Horizontal Hyperbola Given in Standard Form
examples.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $\dfrac{(x+2)^2}{18} - \dfrac{(y+7)^2}{32} = 1.$
examples.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is

$$
\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y-k=\pm \dfrac{b}{a}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k) = (-2,-7),\qquad a=\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}, \qquad b=\sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}.
$$

 

Therefore, the asymptotes are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}y+7 & =\pm (\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{2}})(x+2) \\ y+7 & =\pm \frac{4}{3}(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$
